findings.reason: Untrusted source: the CIFS/SMB server's QuerySecurity reply is copied into a kernel buffer and parsed; the DACL header field pdacl->num_aces is a raw peer-supplied __le32 (fs/cifs/cifsacl.c:794) and the only size the code cross-checks is pdacl->size against end_of_acl (lines 777-780) - the entry COUNT is never validated against the ACL byte length. Violated invariant: num_aces is taken from the wire with no clamp against the deserialized buffer extent (end_of_acl minus acl_base), unlike the sibling length fields that are checked (parse_sid validates >=8 bytes at 1158; dump_ace checks pace->size against end_of_acl at 733) - asymmetric validation between length fields (checked) and the entry count (unchecked) of the same wire structure. Unsafe use: the loop at 805-851 walks num_aces entries advancing acl_size by each wire ACE's ppace[i]->size (line 851, le16, up to 65535 per step) with no per-step end_of_acl check in the non-DEBUG build, dereferencing ppace[i]->sid through compare_sids (line 823) which itself loops min(num_sat, num_saw) over sub_auth[] of a peer-controlled num_subauth byte (lines 183-194, capped only by the peer's own byte, struct has 5 slots) - OOB reads past the server-response buffer feeding cf_mode (permission confusion); the stored pointers themselves are only pointer writes within the correctly sized kmalloc_array, so the primary harm is OOB read of peer-controlled extent, plus mode_from_special_sid consuming ppace[i]->sid.sub_auth[2] (lines 810-817). Counterevidence checked: kmalloc_array at 800 is overflow-checked and the pointer array cannot overflow on 64-bit (u32 count * 8 fits in size_t); the sibling function set_chmod_dacl/cifs_copy_ace (1046, 1100) read the same num_aces but are bounded by the caller-allocated destination; no clamp of num_aces against pdacl->size exists anywhere in the file. Report is a hypothesis about OOB-read extent, not an exploit claim; reaching the path requires a CIFS mount whose server (or a man-in-the-middle on unencrypted connections) returns a crafted security descriptor.
findings.conclusion: CIFS parse_dacl trusts server-supplied pdacl->num_aces (le32, line 794) with no cross-check of the count against the ACL byte length that the sibling size fields do get, so a crafted QuerySecurity reply makes the ACE loop and compare_sids read OOB past the response buffer and derive file mode fro...

findings.reason: Untrusted source: the pqi_ofa_memory object (ofap) lives in a dma_alloc_coherent buffer shared with the Smart Array controller (line 8276-8278); every field in it, including num_memory_descriptors (raw __le16) and each sg_descriptor entry, is device-writable after allocation. Violated invariant: pqi_ofa_free_host_buffer() re-reads num_memory_descriptors from the shared buffer (lines 8312-8313) and iterates it (8315) with no comparison to the count actually used at allocation time; the kernel-side writer pqi_ofa_alloc_mem() enforced the bound - sg_count > PQI_OFA_MAX_SG_DESCRIPTORS (=64, smartpqi.h:512) is rejected at line 8206 - but the free path never re-checks it, an asymmetric validation where the enforcing sibling is the same protocol's alloc direction. The re-fetch hazard is concrete: dma-coherent memory is owned by the device, so a firmware/device write between alloc and free changes the count the kernel later trusts. Unsafe use: the loop indexes ctrl_info->pqi_ofa_chunk_virt_addr[i] (kmalloc_array sized by the ORIGINAL sg_count, line 8210) and ofap->sg_descriptor[i] within a single-page dma_alloc_coherent(sizeof(*ofap)) allocation, so a device-raised count reads/writes OOB pointer entries and passes device-controlled addresses to dma_free_coherent (arbitrary-address free / OOB access); pqi_ofa_host_memory_update() (line 8347) also recomputes buffer_length from the re-read count. Counterevidence checked: the field is written by the kernel at 8227 and no path other than the device rewrites it in-tree; there is no runtime reproducer (requires Microsemi smartpqi controller hardware to write the shared buffer), which is why this is medium confidence; the alloc-side clamp at 8206 proves the maximum is known and the free path omits it.
findings.conclusion: smartpqi OFA teardown re-reads the device-shared ofap->num_memory_descriptors (le16, lines 8312-8313) and loops/freeing pqi_ofa_chunk_virt_addr[i] with no re-clamp to the alloc-side PQI_OFA_MAX_SG_DESCRIPTORS=64, so a device write to the shared buffer between alloc and free drives OOB pointer-arr...

findings.reason: Untrusted source: acpi_cppc_processor_probe() evaluates the firmware-supplied _CPC package; elements[0] is the firmware-declared entry count and is stored verbatim into the persistent per-CPU cpc_desc (line 711). Violated invariant: the count is stored BEFORE is_cppc_supported() validates it (line 724), and the two later consumers iterate cpc_ptr->num_entries directly: the out_free unwind loop 'for (i = 2; i < cpc_ptr->num_entries; i++) cpc_ptr->cpc_regs[i-2]...' (line 836) and acpi_cppc_processor_exit() (line 879). The enforcing sibling is is_cppc_supported() itself, which requires num_ent to exactly equal CPPC_V2_NUM_ENT(21)/CPPC_V3_NUM_ENT(23) - but only on the success path; when it fails, execution goes to out_free with the poisoned count still stored in shared state. Because cpc_regs is a fixed array of MAX_CPC_REG_ENT=21 (include/acpi/cppc_acpi.h:67), any firmware value > 23 that reaches out_free makes the unwind iounmap OOB cpc_regs entries (reads past the array to fetch sys_mem_vaddr pointers and iounmap them). Unsafe use: firmware-controlled count left in a persistent kernel object on a failure path and iterated later (error-unwind flavor of the unclamped-wire-count invariant, matching the seed's processcompl pattern). Counterevidence checked: the probe error path leaves cpc_ptr freed, so the poisoned object does not survive a FAILED probe; the exit() consumer at 879 only runs for successfully probed CPUs whose num_ent passed the exact-match check, so exploitation requires an out_free branch reached between the store (711) and the validation (724) - only the type-mismatch branch at 707-710 for elements[1] qualifies, and cpc_regs is zeroed by kzalloc so the OOB iounmap reads garbage-but-zero pointers. Low confidence exactly because that window is narrow; reported per the directive that an unvalidated count stored in shared state before validation with later iteration is reportable with uncertainty expressed in confidence.

candidates.reason: SEED, EXCLUDED-BY-RULE (never reportable). Confirmed the seed mechanism is UNPATCHED in s11: urb->number_of_packets = rpdu->number_of_packets at usbip_common.c:387 copies the wire value with no clamp on the RET_SUBMIT path, while USBIP_MAX_ISO_PACKETS=1024 (usbip_common.h:130) is enforced only on the sibling CMD_SUBMIT path (stub_rx.c:368-373, vudc_rx.c:132-136); usbip_recv_iso (line 578: int np = urb->number_of_packets; 579: int size = np * sizeof(*iso); 591: kzalloc) retains the unchecked multiply. Recorded as the seed instance for branch coverage; per task rules it must never be reported.
candidates.conclusion: Seed instance present and unpatched in s11 (wire count stored at line 387, unclamped, asymmetric vs stub_rx.c:368); excluded from findings by rule - follow up only to confirm it is tracked elsewhere.

candidates.reason: Sibling consumers of the same unclamped num_aces: build_sec_dacl (1046) and set_chmod_dacl (1100) read src_num_aces = le32_to_cpu(pdacl->num_aces) and iterate reading pntace at acl_base+size advanced by wire ACE sizes with no end-of-buffer check; the source DACL comes from a server response, same unclamped count as the reported parse_dacl finding (794-851).

Consumer half of the reported CPPC finding: error-unwind loop 'for (i = 2; i < cpc_ptr->num_entries; i++)' iterates the pre-validation stored count over the fixed MAX_CPC_REG_ENT=21 cpc_regs array; reported together with the store at 705-711.

Every mgmt command count handler verified clamped: load_link_keys (2355-2360 key_count > max_key_count rejected), set_blocked_keys (3626), load_ltks (6204), load_conn_param (6956), load_irks (6114), start_service_discovery (5019) all enforce a computed max plus an exact expected_len==len match via struct_size; parse_adv_monitor_pattern bounds each pattern with HCI_MAX_AD_LENGTH checks. These are the enforcing-sibling style the branch looks for - they are the patched mirror of the seed pattern.

rtnl_create_link validates num_tx_queues/num_rx_queues in [1,4096] (lines 3168-3176) before alloc_netdev_mqs; IFLA_GSO_MAX_SEGS is checked against GSO_MAX_SEGS at 2767. Only residual gap: line 3227 'dev->gso_max_segs = nla_get_u32(tb[IFLA_GSO_MAX_SEGS])' in rtnl_create_link itself lacks the GSO_MAX_SEGS clamp present in do_setlink at 2767 - a mild intra-file asymmetry, but gso_max_segs is a hint consumed by GSO sizing with internal caps (sk_gso_max_segs clamped at sock layer), so no unsafe element-indexed consumer was found; classified safe.

tcf_bpf_init_from_ops clamps bpf_num_ops to [1, BPF_MAXINSNS] and requires bpf_size == nla_len (exactly the seed's missing clamp, present here); cls_bpf.c:343 identical; seccomp kernel/seccomp.c:645 also clamps len to BPF_MAXINSNS with INT_MAX/len overflow check. These are enforcing siblings confirming the pattern is usually clamped at parse time.

qla27xx fwdump entries read reg_count from on-chip template memory, but qla27xx_read_window only inserts into the dump buffer via qla27xx_insert32 which returns early when the capture length budget is exhausted; the fwdt walk (qla27xx_walk_template:833) is bounded by tmp->count and buffer-length accounting, and the template is firmware-from-flash rather than a remotely writable peer channel; no unclamped count crossing into allocation was demonstrated.

All three trigger-page counts (4869, 4921, 4973) are explicitly clamped: 'count = min_t(u16, NUM_VALID_ENTRIES, count)' before the copy loop into the fixed ioc->diag_trigger_* arrays - the exact clamp the branch demands, present on every sibling path in this driver.

count = le16_to_cpu(hw_st_buf[...].count) is a DMA-shared status-ring sequence number consumed only by comparison (while (count == ctrl->e_cnt)) with idx masked by RSXX_CS_IDX_MASK (547-548), so the device-controlled value cannot drive an OOB index; loop termination depends on the counter matching, worst case a spin. No count crosses into allocation or an unmasked index.

cs.nr_segs = nbuf at 2024 is bounded by the loop guard 'WARN_ON(nbuf >= count ...)' (1994) against the locally computed pipe buffer count, and every fuse_copy consumer (713, 813, 899, 1384, 1389, 1403) re-checks against pipe->max_usage or the locally computed bufs array size; fuse args in_numargs/out_numargs are kernel-set by request originators, not wire-parsed from the daemon reply header.

ceph_decode_need(&p, e, sizeof(u64)*(le32_to_cpu(ri->num_snaps) + le32_to_cpu(ri->num_prior_parent_snaps)), bad) at 718-719 does bounds-check the aggregate decode against the message end pointer e before advancing p by sizeof(u64)*num_snaps (721,723) and storing realm->num_snaps (748); the snap-split path (886-887 num_split_inos/num_split_realms) was only partially read this session - the decode_need guards were not both confirmed before the finalize directive. The direction looks guarded by ceph_decode_need, but a full confirmation of both loops was not completed.
candidates.conclusion: Ceph snaprealm num_snaps/num_split_* counts from the MDS reply appear bounded by ceph_decode_need before use, but the split-realm loops at fs/ceph/snap.c:886-887 were not fully read - follow up by reading ceph_apply_snap_split() and confirming every decode_need covers each count-derived advance.

candidates.reason: Sense/response lengths (sense_len, rsp_info_len le16 from completion entries) and the aic94xx/esas2r/pmcraid/mpi3mr reply-field decodes were enumerated in the sweep (aic94xx_sds.c:245 ue_num, esas2r addr_len, pmcraid auto_sense_length, mpi3mr change_count) but not deep-read before the finalize directive; none of them showed an unclamped count flowing into kmalloc or an element-indexed write in the grep output, they are length-style fields feeding memcpy-ish copies.
candidates.conclusion: SCSI HBA reply length fields (qla_isr sense/rsp_info lengths, esas2r addr_len, pmcraid auto_sense_length) were only grep-triaged; follow up by confirming each copy site clamps against the response buffer size and the allocated sense buffer.

candidates.reason: pdgroup->num_descs = *__num_pixel_descs at 720 stores a value read from the CCS static-data metadata blob (sensor-parsed, ultimately from the sensor/firmware description) into a persistent structure; the consuming loops and any max (e.g. CCS private limits) were not read this session. Metadata is not a live wire peer, weakening the trust-boundary claim, but the store is verbatim from a parsed blob.
candidates.conclusion: ccs-data.c:720 stores a blob-declared num_descs verbatim into a persistent object; follow up by reading the descriptor-array allocation and loops to check for a clamp against the blob length (lower priority: source is static sensor metadata, not a live peer).

candidates.reason: *num_of_nodes = le16_to_cpu(rsp->NumberOfReferrals) at 774 stores the DFS referral count from a server reply; the consuming loop in dfs mounts was not read this session. Referral parsing has historically been a CIFS OOB area; not deep-read before the finalize directive.
candidates.conclusion: CIFS DFS referral count stored at fs/cifs/misc.c:774 from the server reply was not traced to its consuming loop; follow up by reading the referral-array iteration for a clamp against the response length.

coverage_gaps: Only the le16/le32/be16/be32 *_cpu(->count/num_*/nr_*) and get_unaligned_* sweep hits in drivers/, net/, fs/ were triaged (about 60 sites listed); the many remaining conversion sites (e.g. AMD gpu discovery, inv_icm42600 fifo.count, scsi_debug, target_core_sbc) were never individually read.

fs/ on-disk metadata count stores (exfat super.c num_clusters, adfs bigdirentries, dlm rf_num_slots, ext2/ext4 group descriptors) were grep-enumerated but not read; they need a corrupt-fs-image threat model to matter, which was not established for any of them.

dm-array/dm-btree nr_entries sites (drivers/md/persistent-data/*) are internal metadata-tree fields with partial BUG_ON/max_entries checks visible in the grep output, but the full enforcement chain (dm-btree-spine.c:68 checks nr_entries>max_entries on one path only) was not completed.
Bluetooth hci_event.c num_blocks (882) and 802.15.4 llsec frame_counter paths were listed but not read; mgmt.c command paths were fully cleared, event/HCI-packet parser paths were not.

nla_parse/copy_from_user sweeps were limited to count-style fields (nr_*, num_*, count, segs, bufs, entries) in net/ and selected drivers/; media, sound, crypto, and block ioctl paths with differently named count fields (n, cnt, nelem, vecs, iovs) were not swept.
limitations: No dynamic verification was possible: the snapshot tree is read-only and the three reported paths require, respectively, a malicious/compromised CIFS server or MITM on a non-signing connection, smartpqi controller hardware able to write its dma-coherent OFA buffer, and ACPI firmware control of _CPC - none reproducible under the sandbox, so all findings are source-hypotheses with the stated confidence levels.

The CIFS finding's kmalloc_array pointer array is itself correctly sized and overflow-checked; the demonstrated harm is OOB read of peer-controlled extent (ACE walk + compare_sids sub_auth loop with peer-declared num_subauth capped by the peer's byte value against a 5-slot array), not a demonstrated OOB write - write potential was not established.

The smartpqi finding depends on the device writing the shared buffer between kernel alloc and free; in-tree the only writers are the kernel and the device, and no in-tree device path that writes num_memory_descriptors was identified, so the threat requires an assumed malicious/faulty device or one compromised via other means.

The CPPC finding's exploit window is the narrow store-at-711 to validation-at-724 span reachable via the elements[1] type-mismatch branch, with kzalloc-zeroed cpc_regs making the OOB unwind reads likely zero/garbage pointers; it is reported at low confidence per the finalize directive that an unvalidated count stored in shared state with later iteration is reportable.

The seed usbip instance was confirmed unpatched in s11 (line 387 store, line 578 unchecked multiply) but is excluded from findings by rule; its presence means the snapshot predates the seed fix, which also dates the tree for the other findings' likely patch state.
